cap: Prolactin is the one anterior pituitary hormone held down rather than driven: dopamine from the hypothalamus brakes the lactotroph constantly. Anything that blocks D2 receptors, cuts the stalk or adds TRH lifts the brake, and prolactin then suppresses GnRH, which is why hyperprolactinemia presents as amenorrhea, infertility and low libido. Dopamine agonists put the brake back on.
teach: Before calling a high prolactin a prolactinoma, walk down the left box: a pregnancy test, a medication list (antipsychotics, metoclopramide), a TSH and a creatinine rule out the common non-tumor causes. A mass with only a modest prolactin rise points to stalk compression rather than a prolactinoma.
